newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell $66, up $1 - feedlots.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Plains fed cattle sell $66, up $1 - feedlots.

text.p: U.S. Plains feedlot cattle near midday Thursday were actively trading at $66.00 per cwt, up $1.00 from Wednesday, USDA and feedlot sources said.
About 16,000 head sold in the Texas Panhandle and about 8,000 in Kansas, USDA confirmed.
Week-to-date sales in the Panhandle area were pegged at 98,600 head and Kansas weekly sales to date were estimated at 73,900, USDA said.
Feedlot sources said major beef packers were strong buyers early and paid $66.00 for underfinished cattle to augment recent cattle purchases because of strong demand for beef.
The strong beef demand also resulted in early shipments of cattle sold last week and on Wednesday, they said.
Fed cattle prices also were supported by smaller numbers of market-ready cattle on showlists, compared with a week ago and continued light weights compared with a year ago, the feedlot sources said.
Average cattle weights for the week ended February 15 were 14 lbs lighter than last year, USDA statistics showed.
Panhandle showlists this week were estimated near 77,500 head, down 9,000 from a week ago and Kansas showlists were pegged near 75,300, down 13,000 from last week, sources said.
